product.name: SwipePix
product.tagline: The 100% Offline, Privacy-First Android Photo & Video Decluttering App
product.summary: A local-first, offline Android gallery and storage declutter application that lets you triage thousands of photos and videos through fluid swipe gestures or long-press multi-selection — 100% offline with zero cloud, zero trackers, and native system trash safety.

developer.name: Vinay
developer.bio: Independent software engineer focused on Android architecture, responsive web systems, and high-performance offline tools.

product.shortDescription: Clean your camera roll with intuitive Tinder-style swipes, batch multi-select, and an all-new unified in-app video player. Zero ads, zero trackers, zero cloud dependencies, and zero network permission.

identity.typography: System Sans + Jetpack Compose Typography Material 3

platform.architecture: Single-Activity MVVM + Clean Architecture, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin 2.0.21, Kotlin Coroutines, StateFlow
platform.hardwareTestingGround: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (Android 14 / One UI 6.1) Physical Hardware Verified

features.name: Swipe-Based Card Triage
features.tagline: Right to Keep. Left to Trash.
features.description: Review photos one by one in a physics-based card deck. Swipe right to keep the memory; swipe left to stage it for removal.
features.technicalDetails: Custom pointerInput drag gesture in SwipeCardPhysics.kt with spring physics, velocity fling detection, and next-card preloading.

features.name: Adaptive Zero-Letterbox Surface
features.description: Card dimensions dynamically adapt to the exact aspect ratio of each photo (accounting for EXIF orientation). Zero pillarbox, zero letterbox, and zero distortion.
features.technicalDetails: AdaptiveMediaSurface.kt calculates target DpSize from displayedAspectRatio (derived from MediaStore width, height, and orientation).

features.name: Interactive Long-Press Multi-Select
features.tagline: Batch Select & Trash Directly From Grid
features.description: Long-press any thumbnail in the gallery or album grid to activate Selection Mode. Tap items to toggle, tap Select All, and batch trash directly with 1 tap.
features.technicalDetails: Modifier.combinedClickable in PhotoGrid.kt, 0.93f scale-down animation, circular badge checkmarks, and MediaStore.createTrashRequest batching.

features.name: Next-Gen Liquid Glass Photo Viewer
features.description: Immersive dark canvas (#080A0F) with real-time blurred atmospheric glow of the active photo, floating liquid glass chrome, interactive zoom pill (1.0x to 5.0x), 2.5x expand toggle, floating EXIF metadata card, and synchronized quick-scrub filmstrip.
features.technicalDetails: PhotoViewerScreen.kt with HorizontalPager, ZoomableImage pointer gestures, FastOutSlowInEasing animated zoom, and two-way filmstrip LazyRow synchronization.

features.name: Native Android Favorite Sync
features.description: Favorite photos directly from the viewer. Synchronizes with Android's official MediaStore favorite system so your favorites reflect across all device apps.

features.name: Chronological 4-Column Gallery
features.description: High-performance date-grouped photo and video grid with sticky relative date headers (Today, Yesterday, and formatted dates).
features.technicalDetails: Compose LazyVerticalGrid with stable Content URI keys, cursor pagination, and DateUtils local timezone grouping.

features.name: 2-Column Album Exploration
features.description: Explore all media folders and system albums with preview covers and exact photo and video counts.
features.technicalDetails: Aggregated MediaStore bucket query via MediaStoreDataSource.queryAlbums with cover preview extraction.

features.name: Album-Scoped Cleaning Sessions
features.description: Clean a specific album (WhatsApp, Screenshots, Downloads, Camera) or your entire library without mixing progress.
features.technicalDetails: Session and decision isolation via albumId and sessionId in Room database tables cleaning_sessions and photo_decisions.

features.name: Mid-Session Save & Exit
features.description: Pause your cleaning session at any point. Pick up exactly where you left off without repeating previously reviewed photos.
features.technicalDetails: Room database persistence executed inside NonCancellable + Dispatchers.IO to protect write transactions during composable disposal.

features.name: Resume or Start Fresh Choice
features.description: When selecting an album with an unfinished session, SwipePix prompts you to either continue from the current card or start fresh.
features.technicalDetails: ResumeOrNewSessionDialog triggered by CleanupSourceSelectionViewModel detecting PAUSED session states.

features.name: Reversible In-Session Undo
features.description: Instantly reverse accidental swipes during a session via a floating undo button or snackbar action.
features.technicalDetails: In-memory SwipeAction stack synchronized with PhotoDecisionDao.deleteDecisionByMediaStoreId and spring snap-back animation.

features.name: Native Android System Trash
features.description: SwipePix never deletes media silently. All staged items are submitted to Android's native system trash confirmation dialog.

features.name: 30-Day Recovery & In-App Trash
features.description: View trashed photos inside SwipePix with the ability to restore them back to your gallery or permanently purge them.
features.technicalDetails: MediaStore.QUERY_ARG_MATCH_TRASHED query, MediaStore.createTrashRequest(uris, false) for restore, and createDeleteRequest for purge.

features.name: Authoritative Instant Media Counts
features.description: Accurate library and album totals for Media, Videos, and Favorites that never truncate on 10,000+ photo libraries.
features.technicalDetails: Targeted SQLite cursor count queries via MediaStoreDataSource.queryMediaCount bypassing in-memory list length limitations.

features.name: Media Filter Chips
features.description: One-tap filter chips in the gallery header to instantly isolate Videos, Favorites, or Screenshots.
features.technicalDetails: MediaStore SQL selection filters: MEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO, IS_FAVORITE = 1, and bucket/display name LIKE '%Screenshot%'.

features.name: Unified In-App Video Player System
features.description: Full native in-app video playback integrated directly into the full-screen photo/video viewer and the swipe-cleaning card deck. Features custom tactile seek slider, playback controls (play/pause/restart/mute), duration tracking, swipe gestures during active playback, and an "Open with" external player fallback.
features.technicalDetails: Custom SwipePixVideoPlayer built on Android MediaPlayer + TextureView with zero letterbox/pillarbox adaptive layout. SwipePixPlayerEngine handles async prepare, audio focus, error recovery, and instant card swipe unbinding. External fallback via Intent.ACTION_VIEW with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION.

features.name: Liquid Glass & Dark/Light Themes
features.description: Custom liquid glass aesthetic with support for System Default, Crisp Light Theme, and Deep Slate Dark Theme.
features.technicalDetails: Jetpack DataStore Preferences persistence, custom GlassDefaults brushes, and LocalDarkTheme composition local.

features.name: On-Device AI Duplicate & Blur Detection
features.description: Smart grouping of burst shots, blurry photos, and duplicate memes using local on-device machine learning models.
features.technicalDetails: Planned for v2.0. No machine learning models or heavy libraries are bundled in v1.0 to preserve minimal app footprint.

problem.headline: Galleries accumulate clutter faster than we can clean them.
problem.details: Modern smartphone cameras produce 12MP to 48MP files. Between screenshots, forwarded memes, duplicate takes, and accidental screen recordings, users hoard gigabytes of junk. Traditional gallery apps force you to zoom in, tap tiny checkboxes, and scroll endlessly. Most third-party 'cleaner apps' are riddled with ads, demand full disk access, or upload photos to remote servers for 'AI analysis'.

solution.headline: SwipePix turns tedious photo deletion into rapid visual triage and effortless curation.
solution.details: SwipePix presents photos as a fluid, physics-driven card deck with adaptive frames that hug exact image bounds. Swipe right to keep, swipe left to stage for trash. Alternatively, long-press anywhere in your gallery to batch select and purge dozens of items in seconds. Pausing a session with 'Save & Exit' preserves your exact spot. And crucially, SwipePix never deletes files silently—it submits staged items to Android's official system confirmation dialog.

compatibility.unsupportedNotice: Android 12 and below (API <= 32) are intentionally not supported. SwipePix requires modern Android 13+ granular media permissions and Scoped Storage APIs to guarantee zero filesystem compromise.

stagedDeletions.details: Swiping left never executes immediate file deletion. It writes a TRASH_PENDING record into the local SQLite database. Media files are untouched until final confirmation.

nativeTrashConfirmation.details: Deletion triggers Android's official MediaStore.createTrashRequest modal. The operating system explicitly prompts the user before moving files.

recoveryWindow.details: Trashed items are placed in Android's 30-day trash storage. Users can restore items from their device gallery or SwipePix's in-app Trash screen.

sessionIntegrity.details: Session pauses and saves are executed with NonCancellable + Dispatchers.IO coroutines, ensuring no lost decisions during rapid navigation or app termination.

googlePlayProtect.details: Signed with a dedicated RSA 4096-bit release keystore. Verified clean with Google Play Protect ('No harmful apps found') on physical Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra hardware.

faq.question: Is SwipePix really 100% offline?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely. SwipePix does not declare the android.permission.INTERNET permission in its manifest. The Android operating system physically forbids the app from making network connections, transmitting telemetry, or accessing remote servers.

faq.question: Does SwipePix upload photos to any cloud or remote server?
faq.answer: No. Not a single byte of your photos or metadata ever leaves your phone. All thumbnail caching, session tracking, and swipe decisions reside purely in your device's local memory and SQLite database.

faq.question: What happens when I swipe left on a photo?
faq.answer: Swiping left does NOT delete the photo immediately. It stages the photo with a TRASH_PENDING status in an on-device database. You can undo it anytime. Only when you complete your review session does SwipePix present Android's official system confirmation dialog.

faq.question: How does Multi-Select and Batch Deletion work?
faq.answer: Long-press any photo or video in your gallery or album grid to activate Selection Mode. Selected items scale down subtly with a primary border and checkmark badge. You can tap individual photos, tap 'Select All', or deselect items. Tapping the red Trash button prompts an in-app confirmation before submitting the batch to Android's official system trash prompt. An Undo snackbar allows instant reversal.

faq.question: What makes the Next-Gen Photo Viewer special?
faq.answer: The viewer presents your photos on a deep #080A0F canvas with a real-time ambient blurred glow of the active photo. It includes floating liquid glass chrome, an interactive zoom pill (1.0x to 5.0x) with a 2.5x expand toggle, floating EXIF metadata card, and a synchronized quick-scrub thumbnail filmstrip. Single-tap immersion mode hides all chrome for distraction-free viewing.

faq.question: Does the swipe card crop or letterbox my photos?
faq.answer: Never. SwipePix features an adaptive media surface where the card dimensions dynamically match the exact aspect ratio of the image (accounting for camera EXIF orientation). The 24dp rounded border hugs the image boundary with zero black bars, zero letterboxing, and zero pillarboxing.

faq.question: How does Favorite synchronization work?
faq.answer: When you tap the Favorite heart button in the viewer, SwipePix triggers Android's official MediaStore.createFavoriteRequest system API. Your favorite status is synced directly to the Android OS, so it reflects across all your device apps and gallery managers.

faq.question: Can I undo an accidental swipe?
faq.answer: Yes. Every swipe can be reversed in real time by tapping the Undo button during your session. The photo snaps back into the card deck immediately.

faq.question: Can I pause my cleaning session and resume it later?
faq.answer: Yes. Tap 'Save & Exit' at any time. SwipePix stores your progress safely. When you select that album again, it presents a dialog giving you the option to Resume Cleaning where you left off or Start Fresh.

faq.question: How does Trash recovery work?
faq.answer: When you confirm deletion at the end of a session or after batch-selecting items in the gallery, Android moves the photos to system trash, retaining them for 30 days. You can restore them anytime through your phone's built-in gallery or directly inside SwipePix's Trash screen.

faq.question: Does SwipePix clean and play videos as well as photos?
faq.answer: Yes! SwipePix features a unified in-app video player. Videos can be played directly inside the fullscreen media viewer and inside the swipe cleaning card deck. You can watch, seek using the precision scrubber, pause, mute, or open with your preferred external player, and swipe right to Keep or left to Trash videos with instant Undo and safe 30-day Android system trash protection.

faq.question: Does SwipePix support cleaning specific albums?
faq.answer: Yes. You can clean your entire camera roll or isolate a specific folder—such as Screenshots, WhatsApp Media, or Downloads—without affecting other albums.

faq.question: Does SwipePix use AI to analyze photos?
faq.answer: In v1.0, SwipePix does NOT use AI. You are in 100% human control of every decision. Offline on-device duplicate clustering is planned for our v2.0 roadmap.

faq.question: What Android versions are supported?
faq.answer: SwipePix supports Android 13 (API 33), Android 14 (API 34), and Android 15 (API 35). Android 12 and below are intentionally unsupported because they lack modern Scoped Storage and granular media privacy controls.

faq.question: Has SwipePix been verified by Google Play Protect?
faq.answer: Yes. SwipePix is signed with a dedicated 4096-bit RSA release keystore and contains zero network permissions, zero downloaders, and zero external code execution. Google Play Protect full-device security scans on physical Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra hardware confirm: 'No harmful apps found' with 0 security risks.

faq.question: How much does SwipePix cost?
faq.answer: SwipePix is 100% free with no paywalls, subscriptions, or ads. If SwipePix helps you reclaim storage, voluntary contributions can be made on our website.
